key_insight: The paper shows that embodied Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models may still retain commonsense and world knowledge from their pretrained vision-language models, but standard robotics evaluation can hide this by mixing knowledge gaps with control failures. It introduces a way to test knowledge more directly through action-based answering.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of determining whether a VLA model truly lacks factual/commonsense knowledge or whether it simply fails at executing the low-level actions needed to demonstrate that knowledge in robotics settings.
method: Introduces Act2Answer, a lightweight protocol that converts VLM knowledge benchmarks into VLA-compatible evaluations.
Requires the agent to express its answer through action, reducing ambiguity between knowledge retention and control execution.
Evaluates how much commonsense and factual knowledge survives after fine-tuning pretrained VLMs into embodied VLA models.
impact: This matters because practitioners need reliable ways to assess whether robotics fine-tuning preserves the broad knowledge that foundation models bring. Better diagnostics can guide model design, training, and evaluation for embodied AI systems that must both act and know.

paper_title: Does VLA Even Know the Basics? Measuring Commonsense and World Knowledge Retention in Vision-Language-Action Models
paper_authors: Nikita Kachaev, Andrey Moskalenko, Matvey Skripkin, Nikita Kurlaev, Daria Pugacheva
